verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu nissayasampanno hotī”ti?
verses.english: How is a mendicant who is supported defined?”

verses.pali: “Saddhañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya akusalaṁ pajahati kusalaṁ bhāveti, pahīnamevassa taṁ akusalaṁ hoti.
verses.english: “Mendicant, if a mendicant supported by faith gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful, the unskillful is actually given up by them.
If a mendicant supported by conscience …
If a mendicant supported by prudence …
If a mendicant supported by energy …

verses.pali: paññañce, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissāya akusalaṁ pajahati kusalaṁ bhāveti, pahīnamevassa taṁ akusalaṁ hoti.
verses.english: If a mendicant supported by wisdom gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful, the unskillful is actually given up by them.

verses.pali: Taṁ hissa bhikkhuno akusalaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti suppahīnaṁ, yaṁsa ariyāya paññāya disvā pahīnaṁ.
verses.english: What’s been given up is completely given up when it has been given up by seeing with noble wisdom.

verses.pali: Tena ca pana, bhikkhu, bhikkhunā imesu pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya cattāro upanissāya vihātabbā.
verses.english: But then, a mendicant grounded on these five things should rely on four things.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṁ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṁ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṁ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṁ vinodeti.
verses.english: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and gets rid of some things.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu nissayasampanno hotī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is supported.”
